---
title: "How do I compare two independent groups using a t test?"
---

## Question

How do I compare two independent groups using a t test?

## Decide which method fits

Choose exactly two groups and verify observations are independent; inspect distributions and missing data; run Welch's t test and interpret the mean-difference interval.

## Worked example: PlantGrowth

```{r}
#| eval: false
d <- ru_data("PlantGrowth")
two <- subset(d, group %in% c("ctrl","trt1"))
fit <- ru_apply("two_sample_t", two,
                x="weight", group="group", independent=TRUE, confidence=.95)
stopifnot(is.finite(fit$p.value))
```

The comparison estimates the mean weight difference between control and treatment 1 in the supplied experiment. independent=TRUE expresses a study-design judgment, not something the function can prove.

## Apply to another dataset

```r
ru_apply("two_sample_t", your_data, x="response_column", group="two_group_column", independent=TRUE, confidence=.95)
```

If the same subjects are measured twice, use paired_t. If independence is unknown, investigate the design before applying this test.

Review assumptions and available input conditions with `ru_plan("two_sample_t")`. A valid computation does not itself verify the underlying study design.
